decisions.title: Should the weekly decision cycle run as a four-session pilot?

options.text: Yes, pilot for four sessions, then evaluate: the cycle gets tested quickly, but the voting group is still small.
Yes, but at a slower cadence (for example every two weeks): this is easier on people's time but slower.
No, keep ad hoc decisions: less overhead, but no regular way to make decisions.

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (00:09:34). Related written proposals: none.

decisions.title: How long should the correction window and the voting period be?

options.text: 24-hour correction window with an advance notice email about 12 hours ahead: fast, and the notice helps people who travel or have poor connectivity.
48-hour correction window: more people can respond, but each cycle runs longer.
Voting period of 48 hours versus 72 hours: 72 hours reaches more time zones but slows implementation.

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (00:47:08, 00:40:03). Advance notice raised by Joel Okomoli (01:25:50). Related written proposals: none.

decisions.title: What approval threshold and quorum should community ballots use?

options.text: Simple majority (more than 50%): the easiest to pass, but it may not show strong support.
Supermajority (60% or 67%): shows stronger support but makes items harder to pass.
Two tiers, as Lord M.E.G.A Zion suggested: 50% keeps an item open for review, and 60% to 70% moves it forward. This preserves ideas but makes outcomes harder to read.
options.label: Participant proposal

options.text: Consent-based, with consensus as the fallback and a route to revisit (Gael Van Weyenbergh): this builds understanding but needs more conversation time.
options.label: Participant proposal

options.text: Quorum: none during the pilot, a fixed number (the host mentioned 20 votes), or a percentage (the host mentioned 10% or 25%).

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (00:51:16). Related written proposals: none.

decisions.title: How many co-editors per DP, and how many approvals?

options.text: 3 seats, 2 approvals (the current site setup, per the host): lowers the risk of a stall, but seats are harder to fill.
2 seats, both must approve (the published Version 1.0 text): simpler, but either person can block a proposal.

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (00:50:23). Concern raised by Stella Alvo (00:41:37). Related written proposals: none.

decisions.title: What happens when a co-editor declines?

options.text: Keep as is: a decline needs a rationale, and two approvals overrule a decline. This protects good proposals from one opinion.
One decline ends the proposal: a strong safeguard, but valuable proposals may be lost.
A decline sends the proposal to further review (Leandra Preston's alternative): a middle path, but it adds a step.
options.label: Participant proposal

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (01:17:01). Related written proposals: none.

decisions.title: Who approves a chapter title change?

options.text: Steering committee or council: quick, but chapter authors may not be heard enough.
75% of the chapter's authors and co-editors, then the steering committee or council: respects the people invested in the chapter, but has two stages.
Full community vote: broad legitimacy, though not everyone has read every chapter (Leandra Preston, 00:59:57).

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (00:57:41). Related written proposals: none in the snapshot (the DP10 title idea came from an earlier meeting).

decisions.title: Should there be an elected council, and what should it look like?

options.text: Elected council of 5, for Desirable Properties only: small and focused.
Elected council of 7 or 9: more diverse views, but harder to fill.
A Meta-Layer council covering both Desirable Properties and the academy: one body, but a broader remit.
Interim council now (Daveed Benjamin's proposal: steering committee minus Kyle Shulman, plus Renad Baomar), elections to follow.
options.label: Proposal added after the meeting

options.text: Also open: how elections run, and what the current five-person steering committee does in the meantime.

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (01:13:47). Related written proposals: none.

decisions.title: Should co-editors be vetted, or sign an agreement?

options.text: No vetting beyond the 7-day account age: open, but gives no assurance.
A co-editor agreement only: sets clear expectations with little friction.
An agreement plus a questionnaire, published but not used to screen people out: gives context for decisions.
An agreement plus a questionnaire screened against published criteria: more assurance, but someone must do the screening, and the criteria need to be agreed.

decisions.raisedBy: Raised by: Daveed Benjamin (01:19:38). The questionnaire was suggested by Lord M.E.G.A Zion (01:20:57). Related written proposals: none.

processText.intro: This is the current process text from https://desirableproperties.org/process, with the corrections that were suggested or flagged in the 2026-11-16 meeting marked inline. No correction was explicitly agreed in the room. The main correction makes the text match the co-editor setup the host described as current: 3 seats per DP, 2 approvals needed, and two approvals can overrule a decline. Other passages are marked where the meeting raised changes that still need a decision. Nothing here is in force. It is a draft for council screening and community review only.
processText.body:
## Header note

Rules last updated Oct 22. Co-editors: ~~both seats are~~ **[+ each seat is]** claimed or filled by an accepted nomination; anyone can nominate a member or someone new by email. Coordinators no longer hold a seat automatically. Every decline carries a note the author can read. Proposals are decided within 7 days.

Basis: 00:49:36 to 00:50:13; status: suggested

## How a change reaches the book

A change reaches Version 1.0 only by one route: proposed on a passage, filed into Gov Hub, approved by ~~both co-editors~~ **[+ two of the DP's co-editors]**, then published in a numbered revision. ~~A single no from either co-editor declines it.~~ **[+ A decline must carry a note the author can read; two approvals overrule a single decline.]**

Basis: 00:49:36 to 00:50:13, 01:17:01 to 01:19:28; status: suggested (the host summarized the room as wanting to keep the rule that two approvals overrule a decline; no vote was taken)

### 4. Two co-editors decide

A proposal is incorporated when ~~all of its DP's co-editors approve it (two on most DPs, three on DP4)~~ **[+ two of its DP's co-editors approve it (each DP can have up to three co-editors)]**. ~~Either co-editor can decline it or mark it considered~~ **[+ A co-editor can decline it or mark it considered; a decline stands unless two co-editors approve]**, and that decision cannot be posted without a note the author can read.

Basis: 00:49:36 to 00:50:13, 01:17:01 to 01:19:28; status: suggested. The co-editor count is also listed under "needs decision" in the draft ballot (question 6), and the decline rule in question 7.

## Roles

Each DP has ~~two~~ **[+ up to three]** co-editors and one coordinator; members contribute. A proposal is incorporated only when ~~both co-editors approve~~ **[+ two co-editors approve]** it.

| Role | How many | Decides | How you get it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Co-editor | ~~Exactly 2~~ **[+ Up to 3]** | Approves (~~both needed~~ **[+ two needed]**) or declines proposals with a note; publishes revisions | Claim an open seat, or accept a nomination |

Basis: 00:49:36 to 00:50:13; status: suggested

**Filling a co-editor seat.** An open seat is filled in two ways. Any signed-in person whose account is at least 7 days old can claim it with a short statement. **[+ Before taking a seat, a new co-editor accepts the co-editor agreement.]** **[+ Vetting of new co-editors: to be decided (none beyond account age / a published questionnaire / a questionnaire screened against published criteria).]** Or anyone signed in nominates a workgroup member, or someone new by email, who becomes a co-editor and joins the workgroup the moment they accept, with no admin approval. (Remainder unchanged.)

Basis: 01:19:38 to 01:23:50; status: needs decision (support was signalled for an agreement; the vetting approach is open)

## Monday sessions

One community session each Monday at 11:30 PT, each with a single job. **[+ Pilot for four sessions: Monday is a listening session; Claude drafts a ballot from the transcript; participants have 24 hours to correct it, with a notice email about 12 hours before the window opens; the council screens it for readiness against published criteria, giving reasons for anything held back; the community votes over 48 or 72 hours; owners implement the result. The pilot is evaluated after four sessions.]**

Basis: 00:06:37 to 00:09:51, 00:38:31 to 00:41:23, 00:48:40 to 00:49:35, 01:25:50; status: needs decision (support voiced, no objection recorded; window lengths, threshold, quorum and the council are still open)

**Passages flagged for review, unchanged.** Participants did not propose wording for these, but the meeting's topics bear on them:
- The principle "Two people agree before the book changes": consistent with 2 approvals; no change suggested.
- The principle "Decisions carry reasons": participants wanted to keep it (01:18:52); no change suggested.
- No passage yet covers chapter title changes, community ballot thresholds, quorum, or the council. These need decisions before any text is drafted (00:51:16 to 01:00:34, 01:13:47 to 01:16:32).
